chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The pregnant woman whose husband dies, her waiting period is the later of the two terms.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a pregnant widow in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal principle of 'akhir al-ajalayn' (the end of the two periods) for a pregnant widow, ensuring her waiting period extends until both the gestation concludes and the standard four-month-and-ten-day duration is fulfilled. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling prevents premature remarriage and secures lineage clarity, reflecting the Quranic mandate in Surah At-Talaq. The narration underscores the precision of Imami fiqh in handling overlapping temporal obligations.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The pregnant woman widowed from her husband, her waiting period is the later of the two terms’.
en.sarwar: 6. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Waiting period of a pregnant widow ends with the end of the longer of the two time periods.’”
